exercises.title: Read the account register
exercises.find: List every account ID and customer name.
exercises.sql: SELECT account_id, customer_name FROM accounts ORDER BY account_id;
exercises.tip: SELECT chooses columns; FROM names their table. One account is one row.
hints: Which table owns customer_name?
Select two fields from accounts.
Sort the account identifier from low to high.
exercises.wrong: SELECT account_id, region AS customer_name FROM accounts ORDER BY account_id;

exercises.title: Return payment amounts
exercises.find: List every payment ID and amount, including all statuses.
exercises.sql: SELECT txn_id, amount FROM transactions ORDER BY txn_id;
exercises.tip: Projection means choosing fields without changing the rows.
hints: Read transactions rather than accounts.
Return only the two requested fields.
ORDER BY controls the result sequence.
exercises.wrong: SELECT txn_id, -amount AS amount FROM transactions ORDER BY txn_id;

exercises.title: Filter the active register
exercises.find: List accounts whose account_status is active.
exercises.sql: SELECT account_id, customer_name FROM accounts WHERE account_status='active' ORDER BY account_id;
exercises.tip: WHERE keeps only rows satisfying a condition. Text values use single quotes.
hints: Inspect account_status values in Data.
Compare account_status with the requested text.
Put WHERE before ORDER BY.
exercises.wrong: SELECT account_id, customer_name FROM accounts WHERE account_status<>'active' ORDER BY account_id;

exercises.title: Include a threshold
exercises.find: List transactions worth at least 1000 AUD, regardless of status.
exercises.sql: SELECT txn_id, amount FROM transactions WHERE amount>=1000 ORDER BY txn_id;
exercises.tip: At least includes equality. Amounts here are whole AUD.
hints: Decide whether exactly 1000 belongs.
Filter the numeric amount field.
Use a comparison that includes the boundary.
exercises.wrong: SELECT txn_id, amount FROM transactions WHERE amount>1000 ORDER BY txn_id;

exercises.title: Combine alternatives
exercises.find: List payments whose status is failed or pending.
exercises.sql: SELECT txn_id, status FROM transactions WHERE status IN ('failed','pending') ORDER BY txn_id;
exercises.tip: IN tests membership in a list. OR can express the same logic.
hints: Keep either of two statuses.
IN takes a parenthesized list of quoted text.
Do not require one row to have both statuses.
exercises.wrong: SELECT txn_id, status FROM transactions WHERE status='failed' ORDER BY txn_id;

exercises.title: Select a closed interval
exercises.find: List payments from 500 through 1000 AUD, including both endpoints.
exercises.sql: SELECT txn_id, amount FROM transactions WHERE amount BETWEEN 500 AND 1000 ORDER BY amount,txn_id;
exercises.tip: BETWEEN includes both endpoints. A second sort key makes ties deterministic.
hints: Test both the lower and upper boundary.
BETWEEN is inclusive in SQLite.
Use the ID as the final sort key.
exercises.wrong: SELECT txn_id, amount FROM transactions WHERE amount>500 AND amount<1000 ORDER BY amount,txn_id;

exercises.title: Read a date interval
exercises.find: List payments dated on or after 2026-10-05 and before 2026-10-10.
exercises.sql: SELECT txn_id, txn_date FROM transactions WHERE txn_date>='2026-10-05' AND txn_date<'2026-10-10' ORDER BY txn_date,txn_id;
exercises.tip: A half-open interval includes its start and excludes its end. ISO dates sort chronologically as text.
hints: The start date belongs; the end date does not.
Combine the two date conditions with AND.
Order by date and then ID.
exercises.wrong: SELECT txn_id, txn_date FROM transactions WHERE txn_date BETWEEN '2026-10-05' AND '2026-10-10' ORDER BY txn_date,txn_id;

exercises.title: Find a name prefix
exercises.find: List customers whose name starts with A. Use SQLite LIKE, which is case-insensitive for ASCII by default.
exercises.sql: SELECT account_id, customer_name FROM accounts WHERE customer_name LIKE 'A%' ORDER BY account_id;
exercises.tip: In LIKE, % matches any sequence of characters.
hints: Match customer_name, not account_status.
The prefix must be at the beginning.
Put the wildcard after the letter.
exercises.wrong: SELECT account_id, customer_name FROM accounts WHERE customer_name LIKE '%A%' ORDER BY account_id;

exercises.title: Prioritize the largest payments
exercises.find: Return the three largest payments across all statuses. Break equal amounts by lowest txn_id.
exercises.sql: SELECT txn_id, amount FROM transactions ORDER BY amount DESC,txn_id LIMIT 3;
exercises.tip: Sort before LIMIT so the cap selects the correct rows.
hints: Choose the descending amount direction.
Resolve equal amounts with ascending ID.
Apply a three-row cap after sorting.
exercises.wrong: SELECT txn_id, amount FROM transactions ORDER BY amount,txn_id LIMIT 3;

exercises.title: Read the second page
exercises.find: Skip the first three transactions by txn_id, then return the next three.
exercises.sql: SELECT txn_id, amount FROM transactions ORDER BY txn_id LIMIT 3 OFFSET 3;
exercises.tip: OFFSET skips rows after sorting. Stable ordering prevents overlapping pages.
hints: Order the full set first.
Keep three rows after skipping three.
OFFSET works with LIMIT in SQLite.
exercises.wrong: SELECT txn_id, amount FROM transactions ORDER BY txn_id LIMIT 3;

exercises.title: List service regions
exercises.find: Return each region once from accounts.
exercises.sql: SELECT DISTINCT region FROM accounts ORDER BY region;
exercises.tip: DISTINCT removes duplicate result rows. It does not count them.
hints: Several accounts share a region.
Select just region before deduplicating.
Sort the distinct region names.
exercises.wrong: SELECT region FROM accounts ORDER BY region;

exercises.title: List channel combinations
exercises.find: Return each distinct status and channel combination present in transactions.
exercises.sql: SELECT DISTINCT status,channel FROM transactions ORDER BY status,channel;
exercises.tip: DISTINCT applies to the entire selected row, so pairs are deduplicated together.
hints: A status may use multiple channels.
Deduplicate the two-field combination.
Sort both fields in the stated sequence.
exercises.wrong: SELECT status,channel FROM transactions ORDER BY status,channel;

exercises.title: Review completed work
exercises.find: List logs with a nonmissing resolved_at date.
exercises.sql: SELECT log_id,resolved_at FROM logs WHERE resolved_at IS NOT NULL ORDER BY log_id;
exercises.tip: IS NOT NULL finds recorded values. NULL is different from an empty string.
hints: Inspect which cells contain NULL.
Keep the opposite of missing dates.
Use IS NOT NULL rather than <> NULL.
exercises.wrong: SELECT log_id,resolved_at FROM logs WHERE resolved_at<>NULL ORDER BY log_id;

exercises.title: Label missing resolution dates
exercises.find: For every log, return its date or the text open when the date is missing. Name it resolution_label.
exercises.sql: SELECT log_id,COALESCE(resolved_at,'open') AS resolution_label FROM logs ORDER BY log_id;
exercises.tip: COALESCE returns the first non-NULL argument without removing rows.
hints: Retain both resolved and unresolved logs.
Supply a fallback text value for missing dates.
Name the resulting expression resolution_label.
exercises.wrong: SELECT log_id,'open' AS resolution_label FROM logs ORDER BY log_id;

exercises.title: Count all payments
exercises.find: Return one row counting all transaction rows as transaction_count.
exercises.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS transaction_count FROM transactions;
exercises.tip: COUNT(*) returns zero even when its input is empty.
hints: This task needs one scalar result.
Count rows, not amount values.
Use the required output alias.
exercises.wrong: SELECT COUNT(*)+1 AS transaction_count FROM transactions;

exercises.title: Count resolved dates
exercises.find: Return total log rows as log_count and nonmissing resolved_at values as resolved_count.
exercises.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS log_count,COUNT(resolved_at) AS resolved_count FROM logs;
exercises.tip: COUNT(column) ignores NULL, while COUNT(*) counts every row.
hints: Use two counts over the same source.
One count must ignore missing dates.
Compare COUNT(*) with COUNT(resolved_at).
exercises.wrong: SELECT COUNT(*) AS log_count,COUNT(*) AS resolved_count FROM logs;

exercises.title: Summarize posted amounts
exercises.find: For posted transactions, return SUM(amount) as total_amount, MIN(amount) as smallest_amount, MAX(amount) as largest_amount. Leave SQLite NULL totals unchanged on empty input.
exercises.sql: SELECT SUM(amount) AS total_amount,MIN(amount) AS smallest_amount,MAX(amount) AS largest_amount FROM transactions WHERE status='posted';
exercises.tip: SUM, MIN and MAX summarize numeric values. Unlike COUNT, these return NULL over empty input.
hints: Filter rows before summarizing.
Use three different aggregate functions.
Do not convert an empty sum to zero for this task.
exercises.wrong: SELECT SUM(amount) AS total_amount,MAX(amount) AS smallest_amount,MIN(amount) AS largest_amount FROM transactions WHERE status='posted';

exercises.title: Compare average payment sizes
exercises.find: Return the average amount for each channel as average_amount, rounded to two decimal places.
exercises.sql: SELECT channel,ROUND(AVG(amount),2) AS average_amount FROM transactions GROUP BY channel ORDER BY channel;
exercises.tip: AVG computes a mean; ROUND controls reported precision.
hints: One output row represents one channel.
Average amount inside each group.
Round the mean rather than the source amounts.
exercises.wrong: SELECT channel,SUM(amount) AS average_amount FROM transactions GROUP BY channel ORDER BY channel;

exercises.title: Measure regional coverage
exercises.find: Count accounts per region as account_count. Include every account status.
exercises.sql: SELECT region,COUNT(*) AS account_count FROM accounts GROUP BY region ORDER BY region;
exercises.tip: The grouping field sets the unit of each output row.
hints: Read the account register.
Group by region before counting.
Keep active, frozen and closed accounts.
exercises.wrong: SELECT region,COUNT(*) AS account_count FROM accounts WHERE account_status='active' GROUP BY region ORDER BY region;

exercises.title: Build a channel queue matrix
exercises.find: Count payments for each channel and status as transaction_count.
exercises.sql: SELECT channel,status,COUNT(*) AS transaction_count FROM transactions GROUP BY channel,status ORDER BY channel,status;
exercises.tip: Grouping by two fields produces one row per combination present.
hints: The unit is a channel/status pair.
Put both fields in GROUP BY.
Count rows within each pair.
exercises.wrong: SELECT channel,status,COUNT(*) AS transaction_count FROM transactions GROUP BY channel ORDER BY channel,status;

exercises.title: Filter busy channels
exercises.find: Return channels with at least 5 payments, with COUNT(*) named transaction_count.
exercises.sql: SELECT channel,COUNT(*) AS transaction_count FROM transactions GROUP BY channel HAVING COUNT(*)>=5 ORDER BY channel;
exercises.tip: HAVING filters completed groups; WHERE filters the rows entering them.
hints: Count all statuses per channel.
The threshold is inclusive.
Apply the count condition after grouping.
exercises.wrong: SELECT channel,COUNT(*) AS transaction_count FROM transactions GROUP BY channel HAVING COUNT(*)>5 ORDER BY channel;

exercises.title: Attach regions to payments
exercises.find: Return every transaction with its account region.
exercises.sql: SELECT t.txn_id,a.region,t.amount FROM transactions t JOIN accounts a ON a.account_id=t.account_id ORDER BY t.txn_id;
exercises.tip: A foreign key links each transaction to its account. Aliases keep shared names clear.
hints: Region lives in accounts.
Match the account_id fields.
Keep one row per transaction.
exercises.wrong: SELECT t.txn_id,a.region,t.amount FROM transactions t JOIN accounts a ON a.account_id=t.txn_id ORDER BY t.txn_id;

exercises.title: Count activity including zero
exercises.find: For every account, count its transactions as transaction_count. Include accounts with zero activity.
exercises.sql: SELECT a.account_id,COUNT(t.txn_id) AS transaction_count FROM accounts a LEFT JOIN transactions t ON a.account_id=t.account_id GROUP BY a.account_id ORDER BY a.account_id;
exercises.tip: A LEFT JOIN creates a NULL-extended row for unmatched accounts. Count a right-side ID, not *.
hints: Preserve the account register.
Group the matched payments by account.
Count nonmissing transaction IDs so no activity becomes zero.
exercises.wrong: SELECT a.account_id,COUNT(*) AS transaction_count FROM accounts a LEFT JOIN transactions t ON a.account_id=t.account_id GROUP BY a.account_id ORDER BY a.account_id;

exercises.title: Count posted activity including zero
exercises.find: For every account, count only posted transactions as posted_count. Keep accounts with no posted transactions.
exercises.sql: SELECT a.account_id,COUNT(t.txn_id) AS posted_count FROM accounts a LEFT JOIN transactions t ON a.account_id=t.account_id AND t.status='posted' GROUP BY a.account_id ORDER BY a.account_id;
exercises.tip: Filtering the right table in ON preserves unmatched left rows. Filtering it in WHERE can remove them.
hints: Begin with all accounts.
Restrict matched payments without removing accounts.
Put the posted condition in ON or use conditional aggregation.
exercises.wrong: SELECT a.account_id,COUNT(t.txn_id) AS posted_count FROM accounts a LEFT JOIN transactions t ON a.account_id=t.account_id WHERE t.status='posted' GROUP BY a.account_id ORDER BY a.account_id;

exercises.title: Route unresolved payment work
exercises.find: Join unresolved logs to transactions and accounts. Return one row per unresolved log with customer name and payment status.
exercises.sql: SELECT l.log_id,a.customer_name,t.status FROM logs l JOIN transactions t ON t.txn_id=l.txn_id JOIN accounts a ON a.account_id=t.account_id WHERE l.resolved_at IS NULL ORDER BY l.log_id;
exercises.tip: A three-table join follows two relationships: log to transaction, then transaction to account.
hints: Start from the work log.
Use txn_id for the first link and account_id for the second.
Filter missing resolution dates after linking.
exercises.wrong: SELECT l.log_id,a.customer_name,t.status FROM logs l JOIN transactions t ON t.txn_id=l.txn_id JOIN accounts a ON a.account_id=t.account_id WHERE l.resolved_at IS NOT NULL ORDER BY l.log_id;

exercises.title: Avoid duplicate payment counts
exercises.find: Count distinct payments having at least one log, per account, as logged_payment_count. Include only accounts with logged payments.
exercises.sql: SELECT t.account_id,COUNT(DISTINCT t.txn_id) AS logged_payment_count FROM transactions t JOIN logs l ON l.txn_id=t.txn_id GROUP BY t.account_id ORDER BY t.account_id;
exercises.tip: Joining a payment to several logs repeats that payment. DISTINCT inside COUNT prevents double counting.
hints: A payment can have more than one log.
Group matched payments by account.
Count unique payment IDs rather than joined rows.
exercises.wrong: SELECT t.account_id,COUNT(*) AS logged_payment_count FROM transactions t JOIN logs l ON l.txn_id=t.txn_id GROUP BY t.account_id ORDER BY t.account_id;

exercises.title: Find above-average payments
exercises.find: List transactions whose amount exceeds the average across all transactions.
exercises.sql: SELECT txn_id,amount FROM transactions WHERE amount>(SELECT AVG(amount) FROM transactions) ORDER BY txn_id;
exercises.tip: A scalar subquery produces a single value that an outer comparison can use.
hints: Calculate the overall mean separately.
Compare each payment against that mean.
Equality does not qualify as above average.
exercises.wrong: SELECT txn_id,amount FROM transactions WHERE amount>(SELECT SUM(amount) FROM transactions) ORDER BY txn_id;

exercises.title: Find accounts with failures
exercises.find: Return each account that has any failed payment, once.
exercises.sql: SELECT a.account_id,a.customer_name FROM accounts a WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM transactions t WHERE t.account_id=a.account_id AND t.status='failed') ORDER BY a.account_id;
exercises.tip: EXISTS asks whether a matching row exists; it does not multiply the outer row.
hints: Correlate the payment with the current account.
Test for at least one failed payment.
Return one row per qualifying account.
exercises.wrong: SELECT a.account_id,a.customer_name FROM accounts a JOIN transactions t ON t.account_id=a.account_id WHERE t.status='failed' ORDER BY a.account_id;

exercises.title: Find payments without logs
exercises.find: Return transactions with no matching log of any event or resolution state.
exercises.sql: SELECT t.txn_id,t.amount FROM transactions t WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM logs l WHERE l.txn_id=t.txn_id) ORDER BY t.txn_id;
exercises.tip: NOT EXISTS expresses absence without relying on a nullable value list.
hints: The absence is in logs, not accounts.
Correlate the log transaction ID.
Keep payments for which the matching set is empty.
exercises.wrong: SELECT t.txn_id,t.amount FROM transactions t WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM logs l WHERE l.txn_id=t.txn_id) ORDER BY t.txn_id;

exercises.title: Compare within each account
exercises.find: List payments above the average amount of payments on their own account. Include all statuses when computing averages.
exercises.sql: SELECT t.txn_id,t.account_id,t.amount FROM transactions t WHERE t.amount>(SELECT AVG(x.amount) FROM transactions x WHERE x.account_id=t.account_id) ORDER BY t.txn_id;
exercises.tip: A correlated subquery can calculate a different benchmark for each outer row.
hints: Do not use the bank-wide average.
Link the inner account to the outer account.
Compare amount strictly above that account mean.
exercises.wrong: SELECT t.txn_id,t.account_id,t.amount FROM transactions t WHERE t.amount>(SELECT AVG(x.amount) FROM transactions x) ORDER BY t.txn_id;

exercises.title: Band payment amounts
exercises.find: Label every payment small below 500 AUD, medium from 500 to below 1000, or large at 1000 or above. Name the label amount_band.
exercises.sql: SELECT txn_id,CASE WHEN amount<500 THEN 'small' WHEN amount<1000 THEN 'medium' ELSE 'large' END AS amount_band FROM transactions ORDER BY txn_id;
exercises.tip: CASE uses the first matching branch. Boundary order determines which label wins.
hints: Work from the smallest band upward.
Exactly 500 is medium; exactly 1000 is large.
Return the exact lowercase labels.
exercises.wrong: SELECT txn_id,CASE WHEN amount<=500 THEN 'small' WHEN amount<=1000 THEN 'medium' ELSE 'large' END AS amount_band FROM transactions ORDER BY txn_id;

exercises.title: Sign posted movements
exercises.find: For each posted transaction, return credits as positive and debits as negative signed_amount.
exercises.sql: SELECT txn_id,CASE WHEN direction='credit' THEN amount ELSE -amount END AS signed_amount FROM transactions WHERE status='posted' ORDER BY txn_id;
exercises.tip: A conditional expression can turn direction and amount into a signed value.
hints: Filter posted rows only.
Choose the sign from direction.
Return the signed calculation using its alias.
exercises.wrong: SELECT txn_id,amount AS signed_amount FROM transactions WHERE status='posted' ORDER BY txn_id;

exercises.title: Pivot status counts
exercises.find: For each account appearing in transactions, return counts named posted_count, pending_count and failed_count.
exercises.sql: SELECT account_id,SUM(CASE WHEN status='posted' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS posted_count,SUM(CASE WHEN status='pending' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS pending_count,SUM(CASE WHEN status='failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed_count FROM transactions GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY account_id;
exercises.tip: Conditional aggregation turns categories into separate totals within each group.
hints: One row represents one active-in-data account.
Each category contributes one or zero.
Sum the three indicators separately.
exercises.wrong: SELECT account_id,COUNT(*) AS posted_count,COUNT(*) AS pending_count,COUNT(*) AS failed_count FROM transactions GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY account_id;

exercises.title: Report channel failure rates
exercises.find: For each channel, return failed payments as a percentage of all its payments, rounded to two decimals, named failure_pct.
exercises.sql: SELECT channel,ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN status='failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS failure_pct FROM transactions GROUP BY channel ORDER BY channel;
exercises.tip: Use a decimal operand to avoid integer division. The denominator defines the rate.
hints: Count failures inside each channel.
Divide by all payments in that channel.
Multiply by 100.0 and round to two decimals.
exercises.wrong: SELECT channel,ROUND(100*SUM(CASE WHEN status='failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS failure_pct FROM transactions GROUP BY channel ORDER BY channel;

exercises.title: Build daily posted totals
exercises.find: Use a CTE or equivalent query to report total posted amount per date as posted_total.
exercises.sql: WITH daily AS (SELECT txn_date,SUM(amount) AS posted_total FROM transactions WHERE status='posted' GROUP BY txn_date) SELECT txn_date,posted_total FROM daily ORDER BY txn_date;
exercises.tip: A CTE names an intermediate result for the duration of one query.
hints: Filter posted rows in the intermediate step.
Group by date and add amounts.
Read the named result and order by date.
exercises.wrong: WITH daily AS (SELECT txn_date,SUM(amount) AS posted_total FROM transactions GROUP BY txn_date) SELECT txn_date,posted_total FROM daily ORDER BY txn_date;

exercises.title: Compare posted and pending exposure
exercises.find: For every account, return posted and pending gross amounts as posted_total and pending_total. Use zero for absent categories.
exercises.sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT account_id,SUM(CASE WHEN status='posted' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS posted_total,SUM(CASE WHEN status='pending' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS pending_total FROM transactions GROUP BY account_id) SELECT a.account_id,COALESCE(t.posted_total,0) AS posted_total,COALESCE(t.pending_total,0) AS pending_total FROM accounts a LEFT JOIN totals t ON t.account_id=a.account_id ORDER BY a.account_id;
exercises.tip: Pre-aggregate before joining to preserve the intended account-level grain.
hints: Summarize each category per account.
Join the summary back to every account.
Replace missing summary totals with zero.
exercises.wrong: SELECT account_id,SUM(CASE WHEN status='posted' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS posted_total,SUM(CASE WHEN status='pending' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS pending_total FROM transactions GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY account_id;

exercises.title: Find above-average account throughput
exercises.find: For accounts with posted transactions, compute gross posted totals and return those above the average of these account totals. Name the total posted_total.
exercises.sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT account_id,SUM(amount) AS posted_total FROM transactions WHERE status='posted' GROUP BY account_id) SELECT account_id,posted_total FROM totals WHERE posted_total>(SELECT AVG(posted_total) FROM totals) ORDER BY account_id;
exercises.tip: An average of account totals differs from an average of individual payments.
hints: Build one posted total per participating account.
Average the intermediate totals.
Keep totals strictly above that average.
exercises.wrong: WITH totals AS (SELECT account_id,SUM(amount) AS posted_total FROM transactions WHERE status='posted' GROUP BY account_id) SELECT account_id,posted_total FROM totals WHERE posted_total>(SELECT AVG(amount) FROM transactions WHERE status='posted') ORDER BY account_id;

exercises.title: Number payments per account
exercises.find: Number all payments within each account from oldest to newest, breaking date ties by ascending txn_id. Name the number payment_position.
exercises.sort: account_id ascending, then txn_date ascending, then txn_id ascending
exercises.sql: SELECT txn_id,account_id,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY txn_date,txn_id) AS payment_position FROM transactions ORDER BY account_id,txn_date,txn_id;
exercises.tip: ROW_NUMBER preserves detail and restarts numbering at each partition.
hints: Partition by the account identifier.
Order within the window by date and ID.
The final output also needs the requested ordering.
exercises.wrong: SELECT txn_id,account_id,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(ORDER BY txn_date,txn_id) AS payment_position FROM transactions ORDER BY account_id,txn_date,txn_id;

exercises.title: Rank tied payment amounts
exercises.find: Rank payments within each channel by amount descending, using DENSE_RANK as amount_rank. Equal amounts share rank and ranks have no gaps.
exercises.sort: channel ascending, then amount descending, then txn_id ascending
exercises.sql: SELECT txn_id,channel,DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY channel ORDER BY amount DESC) AS amount_rank FROM transactions ORDER BY channel,amount DESC,txn_id;
exercises.tip: DENSE_RANK shares a rank for ties. A tie-breaking ID belongs only in the display order here.
hints: Partition by channel.
Rank by amount alone so equal amounts stay tied.
Use the no-gaps ranking function.
exercises.wrong: SELECT txn_id,channel,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY channel ORDER BY amount DESC,txn_id) AS amount_rank FROM transactions ORDER BY channel,amount DESC,txn_id;

exercises.title: Keep the two newest payments
exercises.find: Return at most two payments per account across all statuses. Newest means txn_date descending then txn_id descending.
exercises.sort: account_id ascending, then txn_date descending, then txn_id descending
exercises.sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY txn_date DESC,txn_id DESC) AS rn FROM transactions) SELECT account_id,txn_id FROM ranked WHERE rn<=2 ORDER BY account_id,txn_date DESC,txn_id DESC;
exercises.tip: Filter a window result in an outer query because WHERE runs before windows.
hints: Rank every account separately.
Use date and ID descending inside the window.
Filter ranks up to two outside the window query.
exercises.wrong: WITH ranked AS (SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY txn_date DESC,txn_id DESC) AS rn FROM transactions) SELECT account_id,txn_id FROM ranked WHERE rn=1 ORDER BY account_id,txn_date DESC,txn_id DESC;

exercises.title: Compare the previous amount
exercises.find: For every transaction, show the previous amount on the same account as previous_amount. Order by date then txn_id; the first payment has NULL.
exercises.sort: account_id ascending, then txn_date ascending, then txn_id ascending
exercises.sql: SELECT txn_id,account_id,LAG(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY txn_date,txn_id) AS previous_amount FROM transactions ORDER BY account_id,txn_date,txn_id;
exercises.tip: LAG reads an earlier row without removing the current one. The default for no earlier row is NULL.
hints: Use all statuses in the sequence.
Restart at each account.
Read the previous amount, not the next amount.
exercises.wrong: SELECT txn_id,account_id,LEAD(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY txn_date,txn_id) AS previous_amount FROM transactions ORDER BY account_id,txn_date,txn_id;

exercises.title: Measure days between payments
exercises.find: For every transaction, calculate days since the previous transaction on its account as gap_days. Order by date then txn_id; first rows have NULL.
exercises.sort: account_id ascending, then txn_date ascending, then txn_id ascending
exercises.sql: SELECT txn_id,julianday(txn_date)-julianday(LAG(txn_date) OVER(PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY txn_date,txn_id)) AS gap_days FROM transactions ORDER BY account_id,txn_date,txn_id;
exercises.tip: julianday converts dates to comparable day values. Same-day payments have a zero gap.
hints: Obtain the preceding date within the account.
Convert both dates before subtracting.
Keep NULL for the first payment.
exercises.wrong: SELECT txn_id,julianday(txn_date)-julianday(LAG(txn_date) OVER(ORDER BY txn_date,txn_id)) AS gap_days FROM transactions ORDER BY account_id,txn_date,txn_id;

exercises.title: Calculate a three-payment average
exercises.find: For each posted payment, calculate the average amount of it and up to two preceding posted payments on the same account as rolling_average, rounded to two decimals. Order the window by date then txn_id.
exercises.sort: account_id ascending, then txn_date ascending, then txn_id ascending
exercises.sql: SELECT txn_id,ROUND(AVG(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY txn_date,txn_id ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW),2) AS rolling_average FROM transactions WHERE status='posted' ORDER BY account_id,txn_date,txn_id;
exercises.tip: A ROWS frame counts physical rows, so a three-payment average is different from a three-day average.
hints: Filter posted payments before the window.
Include the current row and two preceding rows.
Partial starting windows use the rows available.
exercises.wrong: SELECT txn_id,ROUND(AVG(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY txn_date,txn_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW),2) AS rolling_average FROM transactions WHERE status='posted' ORDER BY account_id,txn_date,txn_id;

exercises.title: Measure channel share of posted value
exercises.find: For each channel with posted payments, return its percentage of bank-wide gross posted value as share_pct, rounded to two decimals.
exercises.sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT channel,SUM(amount) AS total FROM transactions WHERE status='posted' GROUP BY channel) SELECT channel,ROUND(100.0*total/SUM(total) OVER(),2) AS share_pct FROM totals ORDER BY channel;
exercises.tip: A window over grouped totals can supply a denominator without collapsing channel rows.
hints: Group posted amounts by channel.
Compute the sum across those channel totals.
Use decimal percentage arithmetic.
exercises.wrong: WITH totals AS (SELECT channel,SUM(amount) AS total FROM transactions WHERE status='posted' GROUP BY channel) SELECT channel,ROUND(100.0*total/COUNT(*) OVER(),2) AS share_pct FROM totals ORDER BY channel;

exercises.title: Measure unresolved queue ages
exercises.find: For every unresolved log, calculate days from its payment date to the fixed reporting date 2026-11-01 as age_days.
exercises.sql: SELECT l.log_id,julianday('2026-11-01')-julianday(t.txn_date) AS age_days FROM logs l JOIN transactions t ON t.txn_id=l.txn_id WHERE l.resolved_at IS NULL ORDER BY l.log_id;
exercises.tip: Use a fixed as-of date for a reproducible operational report rather than the device clock.
hints: Follow each log to its payment date.
Keep unresolved work only.
Subtract the payment day value from the reporting day value.
exercises.wrong: SELECT l.log_id,julianday(t.txn_date)-julianday('2026-11-01') AS age_days FROM logs l JOIN transactions t ON t.txn_id=l.txn_id WHERE l.resolved_at IS NULL ORDER BY l.log_id;

exercises.title: Reconcile regional net movement
exercises.find: For every region in accounts, total posted credits minus posted debits as net_movement. Regions with no posted activity must show zero.
exercises.sql: SELECT a.region,COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t.status='posted' AND t.direction='credit' THEN t.amount WHEN t.status='posted' AND t.direction='debit' THEN -t.amount ELSE 0 END),0) AS net_movement FROM accounts a LEFT JOIN transactions t ON t.account_id=a.account_id GROUP BY a.region ORDER BY a.region;
exercises.tip: Gross activity adds amounts; net movement applies a direction sign. Preserve the complete region register.
hints: Start from accounts so empty regions survive.
Ignore pending and failed movements.
Aggregate signed posted amounts by region.
exercises.wrong: SELECT a.region,COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t.status='posted' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END),0) AS net_movement FROM accounts a LEFT JOIN transactions t ON t.account_id=a.account_id GROUP BY a.region ORDER BY a.region;

exercises.title: Quantify every balance variance
exercises.find: For every account, calculate reported balance minus (opening balance plus signed posted movement) as variance. Include zero variances and accounts without activity.
exercises.sql: WITH movements AS (SELECT account_id,SUM(CASE WHEN direction='credit' THEN amount ELSE -amount END) AS net FROM transactions WHERE status='posted' GROUP BY account_id) SELECT a.account_id,a.reported_balance-a.opening_balance-COALESCE(m.net,0) AS variance FROM accounts a LEFT JOIN movements m ON m.account_id=a.account_id ORDER BY a.account_id;
exercises.tip: A reconciliation variance needs a stated sign convention. Zero indicates agreement.
hints: Compute signed posted movement first.
Treat missing movement as zero.
Subtract calculated balance from reported balance.
exercises.wrong: WITH movements AS (SELECT account_id,SUM(CASE WHEN direction='credit' THEN amount ELSE -amount END) AS net FROM transactions WHERE status='posted' GROUP BY account_id) SELECT a.account_id,a.opening_balance+COALESCE(m.net,0)-a.reported_balance AS variance FROM accounts a LEFT JOIN movements m ON m.account_id=a.account_id ORDER BY a.account_id;

exercises.title: Return every regional debit peak
exercises.find: For each region with posted debit payments, return all payments tied for its largest posted debit amount. Include every tied payment.
exercises.sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT a.region,t.txn_id,t.amount,DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY a.region ORDER BY t.amount DESC) AS rn FROM transactions t JOIN accounts a ON a.account_id=t.account_id WHERE t.status='posted' AND t.direction='debit') SELECT region,txn_id,amount FROM ranked WHERE rn=1 ORDER BY region,txn_id;
exercises.tip: Filtering, joining and ranking combine into an operational exception report. Ranking by amount alone preserves ties.
hints: Filter to posted debits before ranking.
Rank amounts within the account region.
Keep every rank-one row; do not break the window tie with txn_id.
exercises.wrong: WITH ranked AS (SELECT a.region,t.txn_id,t.amount,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY a.region ORDER BY t.amount DESC,t.txn_id) AS rn FROM transactions t JOIN accounts a ON a.account_id=t.account_id WHERE t.status='posted' AND t.direction='debit') SELECT region,txn_id,amount FROM ranked WHERE rn=1 ORDER BY region,txn_id;
